answer: At dawn each new agent locks a 500-unit stake bond into a public Merkle tree, and its branch hash joins a thread the network reads. Every 90 days the tree re-anchors: unattested branches expire and their stake is swept to validators. Forging ten thousand fake identities ties up 5,000,000 units, and every exposed branch loses a 10 percent slash, so a botnet sweep burns about 500,000 before it votes once. A sparrow carries one feather, but the tree weighs every branch: each fake stays cheap alone while total cost climbs linearly, so the attacker pays more than the sybil votes return.
